title: config: formal EBNF grammar as the language spec, proven sound
description: Owner, 2026-10-21: "I think we need a formal EBNF that describes the language so that we can prove its sound". Today the language is defined only by the handwritten lexer/parser (js/packages/config/src/lexer.ts, parser.ts) and prose rules in a deleted plan (now in rasl-m8w design). Code and the 'confirmed' rules already disagree (rasl-m8w.1). A formal grammar becomes the single definition; the TS parser and the later Python port are checked against it.
design:
Lexical decisions (rasl-m8w.1, rasl-m8w.2) are made while writing the grammar. Slice forms per rasl-9ze.1: [n:m], [n:], [:m]; [:] rejected. Relevant to rasl-k2e: an ANTLR4 .g4 grammar is one way to get an executable, checkable grammar.

Sound = both (a) grammar unambiguous and (b) parser accepts exactly the grammar's language. Owner, 2026-10-21: "Both. An EBNF gives a language independent syntax. And then parsers can be written against it, and then finally language-specific idiomatic sugar APIs can be layered on top".
Layers: (1) EBNF = language-independent syntax; (2) parsers per language written against it (TS first, Python port), each checked by the conformance corpus; (3) idiomatic per-language sugar APIs on top (in TS: AST facade, DirectiveDelegator, declarative definitions rasl-xlo).
acceptance_criteria: A versioned EBNF (lexical + syntactic) is the language-independent spec; a machine check proves it unambiguous (every valid input has one parse); grammar-generated positive and mutated negative inputs prove the TS parser accepts exactly the grammar's language and round-trips byte-identically; a conformance corpus with expected tokens/CST/diagnostics ships with it for other-language parsers.

title: config: finish connect validation (overlaps, reserved names, located errors)
description: Connect parsing, defaults and cycle warnings are built, but fan-in overlap is never checked: PortChannelRegistry (config/channel_mapping.py:87) is exported and unit-tested only; GraphBuilder (engine/graph.py:468-716) has no overlap check, so overlapping connects silently last-write-win in CopySliceOp.populate. Reserved keywords are not rejected. Graph errors lack file:col and caret.
design: Reserved: rasl, node, connect, type, input, output, segment, defaults, metadata. Identifiers /[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*/, case-sensitive; node names unique; port names unique per direction per node. At most one source per destination element; overlap = error; non-overlapping ranges into one port allowed. Length: both explicit -> equal else error; one open -> truncate to shorter; both open with a finite port -> finite remaining length; both open both variable -> error. No slice: equal fixed -> all; one variable -> finite size; both variable -> error. Error format: `config.conf:12:8: Overlap error` / line / caret / `input[0] already receives from nodeB.output[5]`. Use count terminology.
acceptance_criteria: Overlapping/duplicate destination assignments, reserved-keyword names and length mismatches each fail with `file:line:col: message`, the config line and a caret; tests for each rule.

title: color: strict color-space compatibility and typed ColorNode output
description: Implement the decided rule. ColorNode's output port is declared generic ColorPayload (color_node.py:104), so downstream checks see 'any color', not the configured space. Sinks needing RGB (sACN, DDP, Govee) should declare it.
design: Input accepts any ColorPayload subclass; output type = COLOR_SPACES[configured space], resolved at graph build (resolve_output_type). Identity conversion is a no-op fast path; a missing conversion is a clear error naming both types.
acceptance_criteria: RgbColorPayload port rejects HslColorPayload at build; ColorNode configured rgb presents RgbColorPayload downstream; sACN/DDP sinks declare their accepted color type; tests cover each rule.

title: color: may plain matrix and color ports connect without a converter?
description: Gap between the owner's rule and code. ColorPayload.is_compatible_with accepts any MatrixPayload (frames/color.py:115,212), and ColorPayload subclasses MatrixPayload, so every MatrixPayload port (e.g. SacnSink dmx, packages/sacn/sink.py:69) accepts any color space and every color port accepts raw matrices. The owner's example (sine -> HSL -> sACN RGB) needs a rule for raw<->color edges.
design: Options proposed by the analyst (not in the plan): (a) keep two-way compatibility; (b) color -> plain-matrix port allowed (sinks emit raw), plain matrix -> color requires an explicit node; (c) neither direction without an explicit node; sinks declare the color type they accept.
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks a rule; the strict-compatibility feature implements it.
notes: Source: plans/Native Color Support.md vs frames/color.py:115

title: engine: sliced or repeated edges replace payload type with MatrixPayload
description: Any input fed by a slice, repeat or more than one edge goes through InputPortProgram.populate, which returns Frame(payload=MatrixPayload(view)) (src/rasl/engine/graph.py:391-396). Only the single unsliced edge passthrough (graph.py:883-891) keeps the source type. `connect hsl[0:151] pixels { repeat 19; }` delivers an untyped matrix.
acceptance_criteria: A test wiring an HslColorPayload source through a sliced/repeated edge receives HslColorPayload; mixed-type fan-in into one port is rejected at build.

title: color: enforce explicit color typing at connections
description: The owner's model is built (per-space ColorPayload, frames/color.py:22-497; generic ColorNode, nodes/color/color_node.py:74) but its central guarantee is not enforced: color spaces interconnect silently and sliced edges strip the color type.
design: Owner (plans/Native Color Support.md, undated chat): "IF they dont match, include RGB!=HSL, then a connection would fail and an explicit transformer node would need to be added. Im not advocating for implicit conversions." "range [0, 1] should be fairly non-negotiable". "I dont want a hardcoded ToRgbNode. I want a generic ColorConvert node that I can configure at runtime." Model: strongly typed payload over float32 ndarray in [0,1], shape (count, components); ports accept a single type, a union, or base ColorPayload; conversion only in explicit nodes, centralized via XYZ hub (nodes/color/convert.py). Output space is graph-time config.
acceptance_criteria: Children closed; an HSL source wired straight to an RGB-only port fails at graph build, and inserting `node Color toRgb rgb {}` makes it pass.

title: engine: two classes register as LiteralNode; registry silently overwrites
description: engine/src/nodes/sources/literal.ts:38 @node("LiteralNode","Literal") and color/src/nodes/sources/literal.ts:84 @node("LiteralNode","literal"). The registry Map.set overwrites without checking (registry.ts:33), so the class LiteralNode resolves to depends on import order.
acceptance_criteria: Registering a taken type name or alias throws; the two Literal implementations are merged or renamed; a test covers the duplicate error.

title: server: Govee and LIFX nodes cannot be loaded from config
description: Nodes register by side effect on import (registry.ts:31 @node). server/src/cli.ts imports only @rasl/color and @rasl/lighting, and server/package.json does not depend on @rasl/govee or @rasl/lifx. A config with `node GoveeLight` or `node LifxSink` fails in getNodeClass (engine/src/config/rasl.ts:310) though both classes are decorated (govee/src/node.ts:40, lifx/src/node.ts:43).
acceptance_criteria: A config using GoveeLight and LifxSink loads via the server CLI; a server test proves both type names resolve.

title: ci: build.yml fails on every push (missing root .nvmrc)
description: build.yml (Dec 2024) runs setup-node with node-version-file .nvmrc and npm ci at the repo root. The JS code moved to js/ (pnpm workspace) and there is no root .nvmrc, so lint and test fail at setup-node on every push, e.g. alpha 7787604 run 39712582683. CI currently gates nothing.
acceptance_criteria: CI installs and runs lint/test for the js/ pnpm workspace (and the Python package if intended) under a pinned runtime; green on alpha.
notes: Owner decision needed before fixing: build.yml's publish job runs 'npx lerna publish' on push to alpha/beta/main once lint+test pass, with NPM_TOKEN. Making CI green turns every alpha merge into an npm prerelease. There is no lerna.json in the repo, and the workflow targets npm at the root while the code is a pnpm workspace in js/ (js/.nvmrc exists).

title: config: DirectiveDelegator typing and defaults
description: From plans/scope.md: handlers must hand-roll { scope, ctx }; register() casts to DirectiveHandler<TContext, unknown>; _enterScope/_exitScope are public-internal; no async handlers; hooks cannot emit diagnostics.
design: From scope.md: after a handler runs, children are walked by default with the same delegator and context unless the handler opts out. Handler result is a typed discriminated union: Delegate.children(ctxOverride?), Delegate.childrenWith(scope, childCtx), Delegate.skipChildren(); no casts, no unknown/any. Scoped override: scope.withChild(childScope, childCtx, fn). Hooks: onEnterScope, onExitScope, onBeforeDirective, onAfterDirective, onUnknownDirective, plus new onSkipDirective. Changing traversal or result shape is breaking; no shims. The register-directives wrapper belongs to rasl-xlo.
acceptance_criteria: Children walked by default; typed discriminated handler result (children / childrenWith / skip) with no unknown casts; async handlers supported; handlers can report diagnostics; plans/scope.md deleted.
notes: Layer 3 (language-specific sugar) over the grammar-checked parser per rasl-g7n. Owner, 2026-10-21: "Both. An EBNF gives a language independent syntax. And then parsers can be written against it, and then finally language-specific idiomatic sugar APIs can be layered on top".

title: config: located diagnostics and consumer reporting
description: All include diagnostics use syntheticSpan() (line 0, col 0) though the include directive is at hand (src/parse.ts). W3005 IncludeNoMatches is defined but never emitted (empty match reports E3001). Consumers invent their own error type (engine IRaslConfigError) because there is no report helper.
design: Confirmed: diagnostics have 0-based line/column, a stable code (E/W + number; 1xxx lexer, 2xxx parser, 3xxx include) and a message. Include diagnostics carry sourceId and the include directive's span. Empty glob match and depth-limit severity: per the D8 decision bead.
acceptance_criteria: Include diagnostics carry the include directive's span; W3005 emitted for empty glob matches; a report(directive, message, code?) helper produces IDiagnostic for consumers.

title: config: typed argument values in core
description: Arguments are flat tokens. The spec (plans/nextgen.md) defines bracket lists and postfix slices, but every consumer re-parses them: engine rasl.ts has coerceScalar and parseSliceTokens.
design:
Confirmed: slices are postfix with no whitespace (foo[0:3]); the lexer does not enforce adjacency today. Lists are bracketed and may span lines. Bracket expressions stay separate tokens in the CST; typed values are a view over token ranges, with spans. Allowed slice forms: per the D3 decision bead.

Allowed slice forms (decided 2026-10-21, rasl-9ze.1): [n:m], [n:], [:m]. [:] is rejected with a located diagnostic.
acceptance_criteria: Each directive argument exposes a typed value (word, string, number, list, slice) per the language spec, with spans; engine coerceScalar/parseSliceTokens are deletable.
notes: Layer 3 (language-specific sugar) over the grammar-checked parser per rasl-g7n. Owner, 2026-10-21: "Both. An EBNF gives a language independent syntax. And then parsers can be written against it, and then finally language-specific idiomatic sugar APIs can be layered on top".

title: config: include-transparent directive view
description: Includes are resolved into a document graph, but there is no view that walks them in place. iterateDirectives (src/iterate.ts) flattens bodies into one stream, losing block nesting despite its doc comment. 'include' is hard-coded in parse.ts and iterate.ts. The engine loader (engine/src/config/rasl.ts) walks only graph.root, so nodes in included files are silently ignored.
design: Confirmed (nextgen, include.md): include is core. Resolution produces a document graph; an inlined view is a separate pass. Include paths are quoted string literals; the loader interprets them (globs included). Core sorts matches by resolvedPath, code-point ascending. Loader: (spec, { parentPath, depth }) => Promise<Array<{ source, resolvedPath }>>. parse is async-only and requires a loader. maxIncludeDepth default 16. Visited paths stop cycles. Loader failure gives a diagnostic and leaves the include unresolved. Included files stay separate nodes so each round-trips. DirectiveDelegator is the public hook for include processing. Tests use mock loaders covering success, missing file, depth limit, cycles, multiple glob matches, ordering, no matches.
acceptance_criteria: An AST view replaces each include with its targets' directives in place, preserving nesting; include handling is a registered directive, not a hard-coded name; the engine reads nodes from included files (test proves it).

title: Add WebSocket external:update protocol
description: Add server WebSocket handling for graphId/nodeId addressed normalized vector updates to externally writable source nodes.
acceptance_criteria: Valid external:update returns external:ack; malformed payload, unknown graph/node, non-external node, invalid value, and length mismatch return stable error codes without changing held state.

acceptance_criteria: npm run dev:server -- <config> starts from TS source; ExternalSource accepts WebSocket external:update values; graph can route values into SacnSink; tests cover config, node, websocket, and E1.31 packet path.

acceptance_criteria: Local UDP receiver test observes expected E1.31 packet bytes for values sent over WebSocket.

acceptance_criteria: @rasl/engine typecheck passes and fresh dist exports current source APIs without legacy graph/log/runtime path drift.

acceptance_criteria: docs/web-api.md documents the GraphQL schema and UI mount; docs/plugin-system.md names rasl.nodes.

title: docs: node-author API in docs/node-development.md
description: Add Config class + arg_fields, @config keyword handlers, Directive helpers, the acquire/fill/commit output pattern and read-only inputs. Source: 665edac:plans/config.md §Node Author Examples, 665edac:plans/performance.md §3.2, §5.

title: docs: payload and color type model (docs/types-and-color.md)

acceptance_criteria: docs/types-and-color.md exists and is linked from docs/node-development.md.

title: docs: config language reference (docs/config-language.md)

Source: plans/*.md, design.md at 665edac
Plan files restored to the repo (owner, 2026-10-21: "don't delete the plans"); read the sources at plans/, js/plans/, js/packages/config/plans/ and design.md instead of commit 665edac.

title: runtime: Rust rewrite, stay Python, or hybrid PyO3
description: plans/rt.md recommends a hybrid (Rust scheduler + color math via PyO3), but v2/ is a full-rewrite workspace (~5.3k lines, no PyO3) untouched since 2025-12-13, and a TypeScript port (js/packages, rasl-2bn) has appeared that rt.md does not consider.
design: Options as written. Rewrite if: jitter >1ms unacceptable, embedded hardware, single binary, Rust experience, long-term maintenance. Stay Python if: performance acceptable, iteration speed > timing precision, scripting critical, no Rust experience, tight timeline. Hybrid if: only scheduler/color math need optimizing, keep Python scripts, incremental migration. Recommended: hybrid -> measure -> expand. Targets (Python -> Rust): tick jitter 1-10ms -> <100us; latency 2-5ms -> <500us; startup 1-2s -> <100ms; memory/node ~1KB -> <100B; binary <10MB.
acceptance_criteria: Owner records which engine is canonical and the role of v2/; the v2 epic is closed or re-scoped.
notes:
Source: plans/rt.md §Decision Framework, §Recommended Path, §Benchmark Targets
Correction to an earlier close: only the config language/package is TS-canonical. Owner, 2026-10-21: "the TS *config* is canonical. The python version of the full runtime is still more comprehensive". Which runtime engine is canonical (Python, TS, Rust v2/) remains open.

title: server: expose node parameters and allow opt-in runtime updates
description: No node exposes current parameter values or accepts updates. Pydantic Config JSON Schema may serve as the spec instead of a new ParamSpec type.
design: Spec per param: type (int|float|str|bool|enum), default, min, max, choices, description. Updates opt-in: default set_params raises NotImplementedError ('Node does not support runtime updates'). API validates before calling set_params. Planned REST was GET/PATCH /api/v1/nodes/{id} {"params": {...}}; server is now GraphQL.
acceptance_criteria: API returns each node's parameter specs and values; a validated update changes a supporting node on the next tick; unsupported nodes give a clear error.

title: server: runtime parameter control and dashboard
description: design.md roadmap phases 1, 2, 5 shipped as GraphQL (server/graphql_api.py:142-212) plus static UI (src/rasl/ui). Phases 3-4 (parameter specs, runtime updates) and dashboard features are open. export_node_schemas (engine/registry.py:218) exposes Pydantic JSON Schema per node type.
acceptance_criteria: Children closed.

title: config: nodes own their keywords via ConfigDispatch
description: config.md migration steps 1-3 are built (config/directive.py:20, dispatch.py:79,108, connection.py:60) but nothing outside config/ uses ConfigDispatch. The loader hand-extracts fields (config/loader.py:51) and hard-codes positional args per type (loader.py:270-321). LifxSinkNode's arg_fields (packages/lifx/node.py:32) is dead: a third positional arg raises. JS takes a different route (rasl-xlo); the owner may want one model.
design: Directive is immutable, parsed once; slice_args() returns new instances. @config(keyword, model=) only marks methods. ConfigDispatch is an explicit helper, not a framework. arg_fields is a plain class attribute on Config. Handlers return domain objects (connect -> list[ConnectionSpec]). Two-phase build: parse all nodes, then resolve connections. Unknown keyword -> ConfigError with line. BaseNode owns connect; Graph owns node.
acceptance_criteria: Loader builds nodes via Node.from_directive + ConfigDispatch; arg_fields maps positional args for every node; per-type branches in loader.py gone; LIFX positional target works; config tests pass.
notes: Python config should become a port of the TS config model (rasl-xlo), not grow ConfigDispatch further. Keep the LIFX arg_fields bug in scope. Owner, 2026-10-21: "the TS *config* is canonical. The python version of the full runtime is still more comprehensive".

title: nodes: SelectNode with GateNode wrapper
description: No SelectNode exists (only CrossfadeNode). Introduce one; Gate reuses it for two branches.
design: Inputs input0..inputN (MatrixPayload or ColorPayload), select (MatrixPayload or BoolPayload as integer index). Output matches the selected branch. First non-empty select value rounded, clamped to [0, N]. Stateless; emits latest_selected_frame.with_payload(...). GateNode: false_branch=input0, true_branch=input1, predicate (bool).
acceptance_criteria: SelectNode and GateNode registered; tests show index rounding/clamping, metadata preserved, Gate choosing a branch from a CompareNode mask.

title: nodes: CompareNode with epsilon semantics
description: Element-wise comparator producing boolean masks from two matrices or matrix vs constant.
design: operation in {eq, neq, lt, lte, gt, gte}, epsilon >= 0 default 1e-6, constant_rhs optional. Inputs lhs, rhs optional (else constant_rhs broadcast). Output mask BoolPayload shaped like lhs. eq: abs(lhs-rhs) <= eps; neq: not eq; lt: lhs < rhs-eps; lte: lhs <= rhs+eps; gt: lhs > rhs+eps; gte: lhs >= rhs-eps.
acceptance_criteria: Registered; tests for each operation, epsilon=0 exact mode, constant broadcast, shape mismatch rejection.

title: nodes: MatrixReduceNode and MatrixStatsNode
description: A single-aggregate reduction node for inline logic and a multi-metric instrumentation node.
design: MatrixReduceNode: mode in {sum, mean, min, max, l1_norm, l2_norm}, axis in {all, per_channel (rename per the count/components rule)} default all; input `input`; output `out` (1,1) for all, (components,1) per axis; stateless; norms on flattened data; reject empty frames; propagate metadata/topic. MatrixStatsNode: flags default true emit_sum, emit_mean, emit_min, emit_max, emit_l1_norm, emit_l2_norm, emit_variance; optional axis; one output port per enabled metric; single pass; population variance; disabled ports not materialized.
acceptance_criteria: Both registered and configurable from .conf; unit tests for every mode, both axes, empty-frame rejection, simultaneous sum+variance.

title: nodes: logic-node open questions
description: Three open questions block final semantics of SelectNode and MatrixStatsNode.
design: 1) Max SelectNode inputs (plan suggests default 8?). 2) Should MatrixReduceNode support rolling (stateful) accumulation later? Plan keeps it stateless until a use case. 3) Stats outputs MatrixPayload or MatrixFrame? Proposal: MatrixPayload.
acceptance_criteria: Each answered and recorded in the reduce/stats and select designs.

title: nodes: logic primitives (reduce, stats, compare, select/gate)
description: plans/logic-nodes.md defines zero/non-zero detection, conditional routing and instrumentation nodes. None exist (no Reduce, Stats, Compare, Select or Gate in the registry); CrossfadeNode (nodes/effects/crossfade.py:22) is the closest. JS port via rasl-2bn.
design: Numeric inputs MatrixPayload (incl. subclasses); boolean outputs BoolPayload (1-D, 0/1 floats). Two-matrix nodes require identical shape; scalar params broadcast. epsilon default 1e-6. Tests: shape all/per-axis, zeros, negatives, NaNs rejected, epsilon tolerance (lhs=1.0, rhs=1.0+5e-7).
acceptance_criteria: Children closed; integration test reduce -> compare -> select detects all-zero frames and gates an output; docs/api.md documents the nodes; examples/logic_detection.py demonstrates zero detection.

title: runtime: auto-disable failing nodes in UnifiedScheduler
description: design.md lists configurable auto-disable as completed, but it exists only in the legacy mailbox Runtime (runtime/scheduler.py:155,378), marked deprecated in runtime/__init__.py:8. UnifiedScheduler (used by the CLI) records failures (runtime/unified.py:782-785) but never disables a node. Retiring the legacy Runtime is a natural follow-on; confirm with the owner.
design: Node failures don't crash the graph; configurable threshold (legacy default None = disabled).
acceptance_criteria: A node that always raises is disabled after the configured error count with node_disabled_due_to_errors logged; the rest of the graph keeps ticking.

title: engine: runtime topology changes by background compile and safe swap
description: No support today: no plan generation or swap protocol (grep generation/swap in src/rasl finds nothing). Topology changes need a restart.
design: Monotonic plan generation id; ports and routing generation-tagged. On change: build ExecutionPlan, compile BoundExecutionPlan off the hot path (validate types/slices/count). Swap at tick boundary/idle: pause routing, reconcile lifecycles (keep, stop removed gracefully, start new), rebind ports, migrate buffers. Reuse a buffer only when payload type, dtype/components match and capacity suffices. Push writes never publish into the wrong generation. API: request_plan_update(plan_spec), poll_compiled_plan(), swap_if_ready_at_safe_point().
acceptance_criteria: A running UnifiedScheduler accepts a new plan, compiles it off the hot path, swaps at a tick boundary keeping unchanged nodes running, stopping removed and starting new ones, and drops old-generation push writes; integration test adds and removes a node without restart.

title: engine: BoundExecutionPlan with port-bound edge ops
description: InputPortProgram (graph.py:293) resolves sources by node id each tick, allocates a new Frame and MatrixPayload per tick, zero-fills the whole view, no shared-subexpression reuse. GraphBuilder.connect still carries slice/repeat/repeat_until (graph.py:468-477). MatrixPayload.repeat still tiles (frames/matrix.py:82-86) though unused.
design: BoundEdgeOp: source_port: OutputPort, target_port: InputPort, strategy, src_slice/tgt_slice (count), repeat / repeat_until; route(tick). Strategies at bind: identity, slice view (true view when possible), slice fill into target region, repeat fill (only needed region, no intermediate tiling; cache repeated segments per tick). Detect common subexpressions across edges. BoundExecutionPlan: generation, incoming_ops: dict[str, list[BoundEdgeOp]], schedule, node_runtimes. Edge type check at bind via FramePayload.is_compatible_with.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler routes only through BoundEdgeOp.route(tick) from a BoundExecutionPlan; strategy chosen at bind; identical source+transform pairs compute once per tick; GraphBuilder.connect describes topology only; MatrixPayload.repeat removed; routing tests pass.

title: engine: complete the acquire/fill/commit output contract
description: acquire/commit exist (ports.py:563,594) but diverge: commit takes a Frame and re-checks payload type each call; acquire never rejects a count mismatch on fixed-count ports; only three nodes use it (waveform.py:188, sine_source.py:77, seeded_random.py:74), the rest allocate per tick via write(). No idle-time growth of the paired buffer.
design: buf = output.acquire(count) -> ndarray; node fills (ufunc out= encouraged); output.commit() -> None. Payload type comes from the port spec, never chosen at commit. acquire succeeds immediately; growth on the back buffer at once; publish swap only at a safe point. Fixed-count: buffers allocated upfront, acquire errors on mismatch. Dynamic: amortized growth, never shrink, may pre-size from graph info. Double buffering: front=published, back=writable. Track ports grown this tick; during scheduler sleep grow their paired buffers on the scheduler thread, then clear. OutputPort: acquire, commit, published(), capacity(); state front, back, logical_count, generation.
acceptance_criteria: Every built-in producer writes via acquire/fill/commit; fixed-count acquire(count != spec) raises; dynamic ports grow immediately and the paired buffer grows during scheduler idle; a test shows no steady-state per-tick allocation for waveform->sink.

title: engine: replace 'channels' with count/components everywhere
description: performance.md §1.3 requires removing all 'channels' terminology with no aliases. Ports use count (ports.py:92-116), but grep -rn channels src/rasl gives 124 hits: config keys (output_channels in nodes/debug/sine_source.py, waveform.py), self._channels in producers, config/channel_mapping.py (ChannelMapping, PortChannelRegistry), docstrings in ports.py:477,534 and graph.py. Changes config keywords used by real .conf files.
design: Slices and count constraints are expressed only in count space (row indices). No deprecated aliases. A DMX channel index is a different payload domain handled by mapping nodes.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rni channel src/rasl tests returns only DMX-domain uses in mapping/sink nodes; config keys and engine types use count/components; .conf files and tests updated; no alias keys.

title: engine: tick-cheap runtime and hot-swappable plans
description: plans/performance.md: heavy setup, cheap ticks. Partly built: count-based PortSpec (src/rasl/engine/ports.py:92), OutputPort.acquire/commit with front/back swap (ports.py:563,594), per-input-port compiled programs with CopySliceOp/RepeatSliceOp (engine/graph.py:167,213,850). Missing: 'channels' terminology removal, full acquire contract, BoundExecutionPlan with port-bound edge ops, runtime topology swap. JS port carried by rasl-2bn.
design: Hot path per tick = pull scheduling + node handlers + pre-bound routing ops only; no graph-structure work, no steady-state per-tick allocation, no redundant slice/repeat work. Two plan layers: ExecutionPlan (structural nodes + logical edges) and BoundExecutionPlan (direct port refs, precomputed slice indices, pre-selected edge strategies). Canonical layout data.shape == (count, components) with dtype. Inputs are read-only to nodes; outputs are engine-managed buffers.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed; performance.md §11 acceptance list holds in the Python runtime.

title: engine/server: unified metrics including sink counters
description: NodeMonitor (execution/monitor.ts:11) records node timings and /stats serves them (server/src/server.ts:198-212). Sink sent/dropped counts are only logged at stop. docs/graph.md:90 describes per-node exec time, overruns, sink emits/drops and resample stats under /v1/metrics.
design: Plan: IMetrics { counter(name, value=1); gauge; histogram; timer(name, duration); getSnapshot(); reset() }; snapshot = {counters, gauges, histograms, timers}. Names: node.<id>.duration/.success/.failure; govee.frames_sent/frames_dropped. Budget: under 5% overhead.
acceptance_criteria: Sinks report sent/dropped through one metrics interface; /stats (or /v1/metrics as documented) returns them with scheduler timings; a test proves it.

title: engine: circuit breaker for hardware sinks and disabled nodes
description: Hardware failures need one shared policy: today Govee backs off, LIFX does nothing, and the scheduler disables a node permanently.
design: Plan contract: ICircuitBreaker { execute(fn); isOpen(); forceOpen(); forceClose() }. States closed/open/half-open; options {threshold, timeout, resetTimeout}; opens at failures >= threshold; after timeout ms since last failure the next call is half-open; success resets to closed. Hardware defaults: threshold 5, timeout 30000, resetTimeout 60000.
acceptance_criteria: Govee, LIFX, DDP and sACN sinks share one breaker; a failing target is skipped while open and retried half-open; breaker state appears in node stats; tests cover open, half-open, close.

title: engine: sink resilience, unified metrics and runtime events
description: Partly done: Govee has exponential backoff (govee/src/client.ts:267-268); the scheduler disables a node after maxConsecutiveErrors (execution/scheduler.ts:372) but the default is null and a disabled node never recovers. LIFX only logs send failures (lifx/src/node.ts:162). Sink framesSent/framesDropped are private and logged only at stop. No event bus.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed.

title: engine: remove remaining any and pull-rate reflection; lint for any
description: One any remains in production (registry.ts:11), plus TypedPropertyDescriptor<any> in runtime/tick.ts:59-60 and 13 `as any` in tests. Pull rate is a symbol on the pull method read via Object.getPrototypeOf (execution/scheduler.ts _findSinks); it runs once per run(), so this is a typing problem, not a speed one. STYLE.md:132 names no-explicit-any and no-floating-promises but eslint.config.js enables neither.
design: Pull rates can depend on the instance (SacnSink @pullRate(self => self._fps), e131/sink.ts:161), so the plan's static map keyed by constructor.name cannot express them and would collide on duplicate class names. Do not adopt it.
acceptance_criteria: Pull rate is a typed member of the node/sink contract (no symbol-on-method, no prototype lookup); no any in tests or tick.ts; no-explicit-any is an error and lint passes.

title: engine: typed node config contracts validated at load
description: NodeClass is new (config: any) (registry.ts:11); constructors re-validate shapes (range-map.ts). parseFps is copied three times with different defaults (govee/src/node.ts:26 default 20; lifx/src/node.ts:29 and lighting/src/ddp/node.ts:23 default 30). SacnSink accepts only numeric fps (e131/sink.ts:16,133), so 'fps 20hz' likely yields NaN (not run). parseUniverses is ad hoc (e131/source.ts:34).
design: Use rasl-xlo declarative definitions (any Standard Schema validator), superseding the plans' bespoke createConfig/ConfigSchema/SchemaValidator. Rates: "20hz" = 20, "50ms" = 1000/50, bare number = Hz. Unit parsing stays at the engine edge; the config spec has no unit syntax.
acceptance_criteria: Each node class declares a config schema; rasl.ts validates every config at load with located errors; NodeClass has typed config; one shared rate parser accepts N, "Nhz", "Nms" for every sink; constructors contain no shape checks.

title: engine: typed ports and payload domains
description: PortGroup is generic over port kind (nodes/ports/group.ts:11) but get(name: string) returns TPort|null, so a misspelt port silently drops output (e.g. correction.ts:70). Payload domain is a string (payloads/base.ts:15,31), so nodes cast frame.payload 23 times outside tests. Tests cast as InputPort 9 times.
design: Plan direction: payload domain becomes a typed literal: "matrix" | "color" | "bool" | "audio" | "control", optionally with shapes (MatrixShape {count, channels}, ColorShape {count, model}, BoolShape {count}). Port specs generic over domain; a port group typed by its name-to-domain map. Fallback if literal-keyed groups are rejected: input(name)/output(name) that throw when missing, plus inputMaybe/outputMaybe. Plan sample code is not valid TS: intent only.
acceptance_criteria: Port names are literal types from the spec record; declared ports are non-null and undeclared names fail to compile; read() returns the payload type the port accepts; no payload or port casts remain in packages/*/src.

title: ports: dynamic port names and port discovery
description: Some nodes build port names at runtime: compose.ts:87 this.inputs.get(portName); govee, ddp and e131 take a configurable _inputPort. Literal-keyed port typing must account for them.
design: Q1: how to handle dynamic port names (e.g. indexed ports)? Q2: how to discover available ports for IDE support? (plan lists no options)
acceptance_criteria: Recorded answer that the typed-ports feature implements.

title: engine: compile-time safety at node boundaries
description: Merges the overlapping type-safety plans. Done: logger overloads, port-access casts in production code, most any. Open: 23 `payload as XPayload` casts outside tests, unchecked port names, untyped node config (new (config: any), registry.ts:11), three copies of the fps parser, lint not enforcing STYLE.md.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed; no any and no payload/port casts in packages/*/src outside tests; lint enforces it.

title: engine: node plugin interface and registry instance
description: Replace the global registry and side-effect imports with plugins registering into a registry instance; the server loads its plugin list from config. Add the JS side of docs/plugin-system.md (today Python only), including a plugin authoring guide.
design: Plan contract: INodePlugin { name; version; dependencies?: string[]; register(registry); unregister?(registry) }. INodeRegistry { registerNode(nodeClass, metadata?); getNode(type); listNodes(): NodeMetadata[] }. NodeMetadata { type; domain; description?; configSchema? }. A PluginManager loads plugins by package name and can load a list from config. STYLE.md 4.1 bans default exports: export the plugin by name. Use typed config contracts, not new (config: any).
acceptance_criteria: color, lighting, govee, lifx each export a plugin; server builds its registry from a configured list; listNodes() returns metadata; duplicate names throw; tests cover loading and a missing plugin; docs/plugin-system.md has a JS section.

title: plugins: loading time and version conflicts
description: Open questions from the plan. docs/plugin-system.md lists hot loading at runtime as a goal; this decision confirms or drops it.
design: Q1: load plugins at startup or dynamically? Q2: how to handle plugin version conflicts? (plan lists no options)
acceptance_criteria: Recorded answers; docs/plugin-system.md matches.

title: engine/server: explicit node plugin registration
description: Partly done: node classes self-register via the @node decorator into one global Map (engine/src/nodes/registry.ts:20-38). The server must know which packages to import (server/src/cli.ts:7-8). No plugin object, no node metadata listing, no duplicate-name protection. The two bugs below are symptoms.
acceptance_criteria: Adding a node package needs no server CLI change; registered nodes can be listed with metadata; duplicate registration is impossible or fails loudly.

title: config: empty glob match (and depth limit) warning or error
description: include.md recommends a coded warning for no glob matches, and a warning at the depth limit. Code: empty result always gives error E3001 (parse.ts:160-169, asserted in include.test.ts:110-121; io.ts:26-28 documents it fatal); depth limit gives error E3003 (parse.ts:103-110). W3005 defined but unused. The /[*?]/ glob test is repeated in io.ts:48, node.ts:6, browser.ts:12. Options: (a) W3005 for empty glob, E3001 for non-glob; (b) always an error.
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks; if (a), one shared isGlob rule decides, and io.ts doc and tests follow; depth-limit severity recorded.

title: config: allowed slice forms [start:], [:end], [:]
description: Open question: allow [start:] (plan recommends yes)? [:end] and [:] unspecified. Core does not parse slices; engine rasl.ts:65-96 accepts [n:m] and [n:] but rejects [:m] and [:]. Live configs use only [n:m]. rasl-9ze cannot define the slice type until settled.
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks forms; rasl-9ze design and spec list them; parser emits a located diagnostic for disallowed forms.
close_reason: Decided: slice forms [n:m], [n:], [:m] are allowed; [:] is rejected with a located diagnostic. Owner, 2026-10-21: "Agreed" (to: allow [n:m], [n:], [:m]; reject [:]).

title: config: lexical rules where code contradicts confirmed decisions
description: (1) Comments: rule is '// and /* */ only', but lexer.ts:126 also accepts '#', and every repo .conf uses '#'. (2) Word charset: rule is 'letters/digits/underscores/dots, no hyphens', but lexer.ts:408-421 also allows '/', and '-', ':' '@' after the first char, so 'a:b' is one word and '[a:b]' is not a slice. Options: (a) change code and migrate configs to the rules; (b) amend the rules to match code; (c) decide per character.
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks for '#' and each extra word character; recorded in rasl-m8w design; lexer and tests match.

title: config: sort include matches by code-point order, not localeCompare
description: Confirmed rule: glob matches sorted ascending lexicographic by resolvedPath. parse.ts:172 and node.ts:38 use localeCompare, which depends on runtime locale/ICU, so ordering differs across machines and cannot be matched by other languages.
design: Ordering lives in core only (parse.ts); loaders may return any order.
acceptance_criteria: Both sites use one shared code-point comparison helper; a test with mixed-case and accented paths asserts the exact order.

title: config: parser error recovery and unused diagnostic codes
description: An error inside a block throws to the top-level catch (parser.ts:65-81): the block is lost and its later children reparse as top-level. A stray ']' makes bracketDepth -1 so newlines stop ending directives (parser.ts:173,185). An unclosed '[' swallows the rest of the file. E2002, E2004, E2005 are defined (tokens.ts:91-94) but never emitted. '{' on the next line gets generic E2001.
design: Recovery is token-range based; the token stream is untouched so round-trip holds after errors. Every diagnostic has a stable code and a real span.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: an error inside a block keeps the block and later siblings; stray ']' and unclosed '[' each give one located E2004 and parsing resumes next line; '{' on its own line has a dedicated code; every DiagnosticCode is emitted by a test or removed.

title: config: keep or drop ANTLR4 parser generator
description: plans/nextgen.md commits to ANTLR4 for cross-language ports. It adds a runtime dependency and complicates trivia preservation, while the handwritten parser already round-trips byte-identically. Recommendation: drop it; use the spec plus conformance corpus (packaging epic) for ports.
design: nextgen.md lists as confirmed: 'Parser generator: adopt ANTLR4 and treat the .g4 grammar as the shared foundation for multi-language bindings.' Planned token model: raw text kept; whitespace/comments may sit on a hidden channel but stay accessible; newline is structural. Dropping ANTLR4 reverses a decision the plan marks confirmed; needs the owner's explicit call.
acceptance_criteria: Owner decides; the outcome is recorded here and plans/nextgen.md updated or deleted.
notes: Owner wants a formal EBNF to prove the language sound (see rasl-g7n); weigh whether ANTLR4 serves as the grammar checker. Owner, 2026-10-21: "I think we need a formal EBNF that describes the language so that we can prove its sound".

title: engine: move config loader onto @rasl/config layers
description: engine/src/config/rasl.ts (401 lines) bypasses the AST facade and delegator, reads raw CST tokens, hand-rolls coercion, slices and error locations, and ignores includes.
acceptance_criteria: rasl.ts uses the include view, typed values and declarative definitions; its private coercion, slice parsing and IRaslConfigError are removed; existing engine config tests pass plus a test for nodes in included files.

title: config: declarative directive definitions
description: The 'minimal integration' tier marked TBD in plans/nextgen.md. Users should declare a directive's name, argument types and allowed children and get typed results plus located diagnostics. Prior art: schema libraries; accept any Standard Schema validator rather than bundling one.
design: Confirmed (nextgen §5): the minimal-integration tier is a registration API that invokes registered directive handlers automatically, built on DirectiveDelegator as a thin 'register directives + callbacks' wrapper (scope.md §6).
acceptance_criteria: A user defines directives declaratively and receives typed output and located diagnostics; works with a Standard Schema validator (e.g. zod) in a test; built on the typed values, diagnostics and delegator epics.
notes: Layer 3 (language-specific sugar) over the grammar-checked parser per rasl-g7n. Owner, 2026-10-21: "Both. An EBNF gives a language independent syntax. And then parsers can be written against it, and then finally language-specific idiomatic sugar APIs can be layered on top".

title: docs: v2/README.md with Python-to-Rust mapping
description: Write v2/README.md: Python-to-Rust architecture mapping and crate choices. Source: 665edac:plans/rt.md §Architecture Mapping, §Crate Ecosystem. Only if the runtime decision keeps v2/.
acceptance_criteria: v2/README.md exists or the bead is closed by the runtime decision.

title: v2: Rust engine to parity (web API, protocol sinks, optimization)
description: rt.md phases 1-4 partly built in v2/ (core, scheduler, config parser+loader, CLI; nodes literal, waveform, sacn source, color, compose, twinkle, console, ddp). Missing: rasl-server, sACN sink, Math/Slice transforms, optimization phase, benchmarks vs Python.
design: Crates: tokio, ndarray, wide/packed_simd, palette, serde, tracing, clap, nom/pest; axum, tokio-tungstenite, async-graphql, askama. Workspace: rasl-core, rasl-runtime, rasl-nodes, rasl-config, rasl-server, rasl-sacn, rasl-ddp, rasl (bin). Scheduler: exact tick times per sink rate, recursive pull, per-tick memoization, previous-tick values for back-edges; sync first. Optimization: SIMD Oklab, per-frame arena (bumpalo), crossbeam channels, perf/flamegraph/criterion. Validate color math against colour-science.
acceptance_criteria: v2 loads existing .conf files, drives sACN and DDP, serves the UI over HTTP/WS/GraphQL, and criterion benchmarks report against rt.md targets.

title: server: where to define security constraints (auth, ACL)
description: design.md Open Question 3. The API now accepts writes (JS ExternalSource over WebSocket, rasl-bp3), making this more pressing.
design: No options listed in the plan.
acceptance_criteria: Owner decides; follow-up beads filed.

title: test: loopback sACN integration and DAG property tests
description: design.md Testing Strategy names loopback sACN integration tests and DAG property tests; tests/ has neither.
design: Cycles are warned per dag.md, superseding design.md's 'reject cycles'.
acceptance_criteria: A test sends through SacnSinkNode and receives on localhost via SacnSourceNode with bytes verified; property tests generate random graphs and check validation (cycles warned, overlaps rejected).

title: observability: frame tracing, Prometheus metrics, capture and replay
description: Not built: per-frame trace ids, optional Prometheus export, frame capture and replay CLI. structlog and NodeMonitor exist (cli.py:23, runtime/monitor.py:76).
design: Optional prometheus_client. Per-frame UUID through the DAG. Frames serializable for capture.
acceptance_criteria: Optional Prometheus endpoint exports frames/sec per node, queue depth, latency; frames carry a trace id in logs; rasl can capture frames to disk and replay them.

title: ui: interactive graph, parameter controls, DMX preview, log viewer
description: design.md Phase 5 future dashboard features.
design: Interactive graph (D3.js or similar); sliders from param specs; real-time DMX preview; log viewer/event stream; metrics filter by node id.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows an interactive graph, sliders bound to node parameters, live channel preview and a log/event stream.

title: config: reload config files dynamically?
description: design.md Open Question 2: 'Should config support dynamic reloading? (Could use file watcher, but not MVP.)' Hot swap would provide the mechanism.
design: Options as written: dynamic reloading via a file watcher; or not (not MVP).
acceptance_criteria: Owner decides; if yes, a feature bead is filed.

title: engine: reduce per-tick allocation if the benchmark warrants
description: Each tick allocates TickContext (scheduler.ts:316), NodeContext and child loggers (scheduler.ts:413), and Frames (16 sites). Payload buffers already reuse (FramePayload.ensureBuffer). Frame is immutable (frame.ts:34-60) and the scheduler serves the previous tick's frame on cycles, so the plan's Frame.reset() pooling conflicts with current semantics.
design: Plan pool targets: Frame, Context, child Logger. API acquire(topic, timestamp, payload) / release(frame).
acceptance_criteria: Only if the benchmark shows allocation/GC above target: reduce it while keeping Frame semantics safe; otherwise close with measurements.

title: engine: single deadline-driven scheduler loop
description: Merge duplicated run()/runFor() (execution/scheduler.ts:145-225); replace 1ms polling with sleeping until the next sink deadline. Compare with the canonical Python scheduler first (rasl-2bn).
design: Next deadline = earliest next sink pull across sink rates (not a fixed 60 FPS).
acceptance_criteria: One loop; lower idle CPU and no worse frame timing on the benchmark; scheduler tests pass.

title: engine: scheduler benchmark harness
description: No benchmark exists, so no performance claim can be checked.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable benchmark reports ms/frame, allocation rate and GC pauses for a 10-node graph at 60 FPS; baseline recorded.

title: perf: pooling toggle, regression reporting, TypedArray allocator
description: Open questions from the performance plan.
design: Q1: should object pooling be configurable for debugging? Q2: how to measure and report performance regressions? Q3: a custom allocator for TypedArrays?
acceptance_criteria: Recorded answers.

title: engine: measured scheduler performance
description: The plan's before figures (15ms/frame, 1MB/s allocation, 5-10ms GC) have no benchmark, so measure first. run() and runFor() are near-duplicates (execution/scheduler.ts:165-185, 207-223) and both poll with await sleep(1).
design: Plan targets: 60 FPS with 10 nodes at about 8ms/frame, about 100KB/s allocation, GC pauses under 2ms every 5s.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed and benchmark results recorded.

title: engine/server: runtime event stream
description: Nothing can react to node failures or connection changes; no event bus exists in js/packages. docs/graph.md:91 describes a WebSocket events topic (graph swaps, eos, drops). Carry events over the existing WebSocket, no new infrastructure.
design: Events: node.started {nodeId, timestamp}; node.stopped {nodeId, timestamp}; node.failed {nodeId, error, timestamp}; scheduler.started {timestamp}; scheduler.stopped {timestamp, duration}; connection.established {target, protocol}; connection.lost {target, protocol, error?}; connection.restored {target, protocol}. A failing handler is logged, not rethrown. Typed event-name-to-payload map.
acceptance_criteria: Engine emits typed events at node start/stop/failure, scheduler start/stop and connection changes; clients subscribe over the WebSocket; a test proves it.

title: resilience/observability: configurability and persistence
description: Open questions from the plan affecting circuit breakers, metrics and events.
design: Q1: circuit breakers configurable per node? Q2: persist metrics across restarts? Q3: persist events for replay? (plan lists no options)
acceptance_criteria: Recorded answers.

title: engine: branded unit types for Hz, ms, seconds, ratio
description: Unit-bearing numbers are plain numbers; names carry units (frequencyHz in twinkle.ts:29, frameBudgetMs in scheduler.ts:31) but the compiler does not check them.
design: Brands: Hz, Ms, Seconds, Ratio (0-1 phase). Constructors hz(), ms(), seconds(), ratio(). msToHz = 1000/ms, hzToMs = 1000/hz. Fields: waveform frequency: Hz, phase: Ratio; scheduler frameBudget: Ms, maxDuration: Seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Unit-carrying config and scheduler fields use branded types with constructors and conversions; assigning ms to Hz fails to compile (type test).

title: engine: typed LogFields for known log keys
description: Logger API is done (message first, fields optional; nodes/context.ts:12-24). LogFields is still Record<string, unknown> (context.ts:10), so nodeId, tick, elapsedMs are unchecked.
design: Known keys: nodeId: string, tick: number, elapsedMs: number. traceNode/debugNode helpers are redundant with childLogger (logging/index.ts:93).
acceptance_criteria: LogFields declares known keys with types per the decision; every call site typechecks.

title: logging: closed or open LogFields
description: The plans disagree: domain-leakage gives a closed set of known fields; api-ergonomics adds [key: string]: unknown.
design: Options as written: known fields only (domain-leakage) vs known fields plus an index signature (api-ergonomics).
acceptance_criteria: Recorded choice that the LogFields task implements.

title: types: config validation and branded-unit questions
description: Open questions from the type plans not settled elsewhere. Backward-compatibility questions are settled by the no-backwards-compatibility rule; 'use Zod?' is settled for config by rasl-xlo (any Standard Schema validator).
design: Q1: config validation runtime-only, or compile-time too? Q2: how to handle dynamic configuration (e.g. from JSON)? Q3: should branded types have a runtime representation? Q4: how to handle optional vs required configuration elegantly?
acceptance_criteria: Recorded answers that the config-contracts and branded-units features implement.

title: config: delegator per-directive child context merges
description: Open question in scope.md: derive a child's context from the parent handler's result? Today handlers return { scope, ctx } (delegator.ts:13-27). Planned Delegate.children(ctxOverride?) / childrenWith cover explicit overrides. Options: (a) explicit overrides only; (b) a typed merge hook (parentCtx, result) => childCtx.
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks; recorded in rasl-stq design.

title: config: sync parse with cached resolver, or strict split
description: Open question in include.md. Today: async parse() only (parse.ts:38); sync parseDocument (parser.ts:256) not exported. rasl-m8w already plans a sync single-file entry (the strict-split option for single files). A sync multi-file parse via cached resolver is undecided.
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks; recorded in rasl-m8w design; exported API matches.

title: config: string escapes v2 (\uXXXX / \xNN)
description: Open question. Options as written: add \uXXXX / \xNN escapes, or rely on raw UTF-8 source; if added, the raw lexeme must win for round-trip. Today only v1 escapes decode (lexer.ts:264-282); others emit W1004 and keep the literal char. token.text keeps the raw lexeme, so round-trip holds either way.
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks; spec and lexer follow; if added, a test proves decoded value and byte-identical round-trip.

title: config: release hardening (fuzz, benchmarks, semver, security note)
description: nextgen milestone 8. None exists: no property/fuzz tests, benchmarks, security note or spec version. Add fuzz/property tests for lexer and parser (no crash, round-trip on any input, linear time), benchmarks with budgets for large files, a security note (core does no I/O; include resolution is caller-supplied), semver rules for spec and API.
design: Core imports no I/O (fs only in src/node.ts, fetch only in src/browser.ts); keep it so. Versions only from the automated release flow. Fuzzing covers the unbalanced-bracket and nested-error recovery paths.
acceptance_criteria: Property test asserts serializeCst(parseDocument(x).cst) === x and no throw for arbitrary strings; a benchmark with a time budget is documented; security note in README; spec and API versioning rules documented and wired to the automated release flow.

title: config: cross-language JSON form and porting guide
description: nextgen milestone 7. No language-agnostic serialization of tokens, CST or diagnostics exists, so a Python or C++ port has nothing to be checked against. Define a canonical JSON form for tokens, CST (token ranges) and diagnostics, emit it from TS, and use it as the expected output of the conformance corpus (rasl-m8w). Write a short porting guide: string escapes, newline rules, offset units, error-recovery expectations.
design: Spec plus conformance corpus are the source of truth, not the TS code. The JSON form states the unit of offset and column (code uses UTF-16 code units though tokens.ts:44 says 'byte offset'). Diagnostics carry code, severity, message, 0-based span, sourceId.
acceptance_criteria: JSON schema for tokens, CST and diagnostics published; TS toJson output passes the whole conformance corpus; porting guide in the package docs.

title: config: AST edits via token splicing only, or also a printer
description: Open question in roundtrip.md: expose a stable printer for AST-level edits, or is token splicing the only supported way to preserve formatting? rasl-uji assumes token splicing. A normalizing printer would also be the formatter in the tooling epic. Options as written: (a) token splicing only; (b) also a stable printer for AST edits (may normalize formatting).
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks; recorded in rasl-uji design; tooling formatter scope follows.

title: config: open-source packaging and spec
description: plans/nextgen.md milestone 0 and API hygiene: RASL-centric name/README/fixtures; parseDocument (sync single-file) not exported so the simplest use needs async parse plus a dummy loader; public types mutable; no published grammar. Interface naming follows js/STYLE.md 3.6 (I prefix kept).
design: Confirmed language rules (nextgen §Current decisions): newline ends a directive; semicolons optional, needed only for several directives on one line. No backslash line continuation. Newlines allowed inside [...] lists until the matching ']'. '{' on the same line as its header. Strings use ' or ". v1 escapes: \\ \n \t \r \" \' only. Comments: // and /* */ only (contradicted by code, see D1 bead). Dot is part of a word. Unquoted words: letters, digits, underscores, dots, no hyphens (contradicted by code, see D1 bead). Diagnostics: 0-based line/column, stable codes plus messages. Public API keeps the directive-level AST; no RASL node/connection AST. Core does no I/O. Spec deliverables: EBNF grammar plus lexical spec; versioned core profile; conformance corpus of inputs with expected tokens/CST/diagnostics as JSON. Milestone 0: generic README, RASL examples move to the consumer, neutral fixtures (e.g. server { listen 8080; }). Spec states the unit of offset and column.
acceptance_criteria: RASL removed from package surface; a sync single-file parse entry point exported; public types readonly; the grammar epic's spec is published with the package.

title: config: AST editing API with token splicing
description: README claims AST edits modify the CST, but IAstDirective has no mutators and the token-splice utilities in plans/roundtrip.md do not exist, so save() has nothing to persist. No consumer needs editing yet; fix the README claim now.
design: Confirmed (nextgen, roundtrip): byte-identical serializeCst(parse(x).cst) === x is first-class. Trivia kept in CST. Canonical storage is the full token stream; directive nodes reference token ranges, never copy tokens. Tokens keep raw text and 0-based spans. Serialization is token concatenation; subtree = node's token range. Edits are token splices keeping spans stable; no trivia-attachment heuristics. Three tiers: power users edit tokens/CST byte-identically; most use the AST facade (edits may normalize formatting); minimal consumers use declarative registration (rasl-xlo). Tests: golden round-trip; mutation tests assert only intended token ranges change.
acceptance_criteria: rename, setArgs, insert and remove edit tokens in place preserving formatting; golden tests show only intended token ranges change; save() persists edits across included files; plans/roundtrip.md deleted.

title: config: may delegator handlers mutate directive arguments
description: Open question in scope.md. IAstDirective is read-only today (ast.ts:37-52); editing is planned in rasl-uji. Options: (a) mutation through the delegator; (b) out of scope, edit only via rasl-uji.
acceptance_criteria: Owner picks; recorded in rasl-stq design (and rasl-uji if a).

title: config: tooling (CLI, formatter, editor support)
description: nextgen milestone 6, marked optional. Nothing exists: no bin entry, formatter or editor grammar. CLI: parse/validate/format/print (--tokens, --cst, --ast, --json, --diagnostics). Formatter: deterministic output, optionally trivia-preserving. Editor: syntax highlighting first, then LSP features driven by CST spans.
design: --json uses the canonical JSON form. The formatter is the normalizing printer only if D5 picks one; it never changes directive semantics. Diagnostics use the stable DiagnosticCode set with 0-based spans.
acceptance_criteria: CLI prints tokens/CST/AST/diagnostics as JSON and exits non-zero on errors; formatter is idempotent on the conformance corpus; a highlighting grammar ships; LSP features filed as follow-up beads.
